study.question: Observed baseline-din has macro AUC 0.8099233881, train time 293.065 s and model batch p50 15.2925 ms. Source inspection shows nonlinear target-event scoring on all 100 padded positions followed by one common pooled history. Can target-field-aligned, count-preserving compression move this scoring to eight slots with less loss than position-only summaries? The history_gt64 slice has 1,401,885 samples and macro AUC 0.8273443710; history_1_16 has 461,684 samples and 0.7628409323. These are descriptive population differences, not evidence that long histories cause gains or that compression is needed for accuracy.
study.hypothesis: When mean compression precedes nonlinear target scoring, grouping history by target category/brand agreement preserves relevance distinctions that blind position means mix away. Cross those four mutually exclusive field-match states with two ordinal recency bands, retain all eight projected summaries plus masked slot counts, and let the four task towers jointly interact them with user/context and target fields. Target routing should mitigate quality loss from moving nonlinear scoring after compression; fewer scorer positions should reduce measured cost. This is an untested local hypothesis.

nearest_work.difference: Archived arXiv:1706.06978v4 primary text and baseline_reference.py inspected. Inherit target-key local activation interaction [q,k,q-k,q*k] and field embeddings; replace a single unnormalized weighted sum by disjoint count-preserving slot means and joint slot readout. No exact DIN reproduction claim.

Pinned benchmark forward/tokenizer inspected at 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d. It uses fixed and conditioned queries, recent/earlier partitions and HeteroMixer. Here routing is deterministic category/brand equality, local scoring is moved across group means, and task readout uses projected disjoint slots; mixed learned queries and low-rank heterogeneous token mixing are not implemented.

Original HeMix v3 section 3.2.2 read via public primary HTML (title differs from the registry title). Its dynamic/fixed query extraction is related; this implementation instead tests deterministic partitions and compression timing, using only the fixed 100-event input. Ordinal recent16 does not reproduce original real-time/day-based sequence semantics. No novelty claim.

SIM original section 3.2 hard-search selects same-category events. Inherit cheap target-field equality as an existing relevance proxy. Here retain every valid event in disjoint category x brand agreement slots, including nonmatches, crossed with ordinal recency, rather than retrieving a same-category top-K subsequence. Test mean compression timing in a fixed 100-event, four-label benchmark. General target-aware search is prior work, and novelty is unverified.
Cached primary benchmark section 2.3 read. Unified compression/interaction is established prior work. This proposal is a controlled local representation study, not a new-family or priority claim.

study.proposed_difference: Four standalone, parameter-matched modules form a 2x2 design: target-field versus position grouping, crossed with early versus late mean compression. Target slots are g = 2*category_match + brand_match + 4*recent, with nonzero token equality only; zero is treated as missing. Recent means last16 ordinal history positions, older means preceding84. Position controls subdivide each same recency band into four bins. Every valid event belongs to exactly one slot. Early: mean k and v per slot, then score(q,mean k)*mean v. Late: mean(score(q,k)*v) per slot. v includes all item fields plus historical action embeddings. Shared bias-free v->32 projection is applied after pooling; concatenate eight slot projections, eight counts/100, target and user/context embeddings into each task tower. Empty slot values and counts are zero. No target action or supplied current labels are read. Shared unknown nonzero vocabulary tokens may still create spurious equality; only zero exclusion is established. Compared with baseline, this also changes normalization/readout/local activation, so baseline gains alone do not identify the compression mechanism.
predictions: Primary routing contrast: AUC(target_early)-AUC(position_early)>0; report every task AUC and Logloss delta plus macro Logloss, without an undeclared per-task veto.

Mechanism interaction: [AUC(target_early)-AUC(target_late)]-[AUC(position_early)-AUC(position_late)]>0. A benefit only common to both timings does not establish compression-specific information retention.

Efficiency acceptance hypothesis, separate from selection: target_early macro AUC is no more than 0.001 below target_late while model batch p50 is at least20% lower. Use measured train time, inference throughput, p50/p95, peak memory and total/dense/embedding parameter counts; the 100->8 scorer reduction is an operation-count prediction, not a measured speedup.

Predeclared descriptive checks: the existing empty,1_16,17_64,gt64 history bins with full per-task sample/positive/negative counts; compression penalties are expected primarily in gt64. Empty histories are not expected to benefit from routing; any effect there comes from fitted downstream parameters. Treat this as exploratory after the main factorial.

If host diagnostic facilities are available, check train-defined category/brand frequency and unknown/zero slices, hour, behavior composition, and routing occupancy. Mark unavailable diagnostics rather than invent sample counts or add inputs. Do not infer statistical significance from one seed.

Host preflight must verify all four [B,1] outputs, finite probabilities and BCE/backward gradients, all-zero masks, single valid event, full history, masked-payload invariance, and target-action invariance under the frozen BF16 interface. Locally only syntax/source and pure scalar routing invariants can be checked because torch/numpy are absent.
falsifiers: If target_early fails to beat position_early, evidence does not support the proposed target-routing benefit for this implementation.
If the factorial interaction is null or negative, target routing has not been shown to protect against early mean compression; a routing main effect alone is insufficient.
If target_early loses more than0.001 macro AUC against target_late or measured p50 latency improves less than20%, the declared efficiency condition fails even if scorer operation count is smaller.

Nonfinite outputs/gradients, inconsistent mask or target-action invariance, accidental label use, or unequal learned parameter shapes across factorial variants invalidate the intended comparison; a host preflight failure is an execution failure rather than scientific refutation.

If any apparent routing gain disappears with slot count channels removed or appears in a counts-only replacement, do not attribute it to retained embedded event information. That follow-up is reserved for a later authorized proposal if results justify it.
alternative_explanations: The baseline slice gap can reflect user composition, task prevalence, time or exposure effects; it is not a causal history-length experiment.
A gain over DIN may reflect a larger tower input, slot count features, changed normalization or ReLU local activation; factorial controls isolate their shared settings, not each baseline difference.

Category/brand match-count statistics may explain routing gains without improved embedding compression. Auxiliary labels themselves are same user/category/brand future-window events, not advertisement-specific conversions.

Position groups are contiguous and target groups have different occupancy/heterogeneity. The routing intervention includes these representation changes; evidence cannot distinguish equality semantics from every form of grouping regularization.
Embedding lookup/data loading may dominate measured cost, and eight-slot scatter/matmul or wider task readout can erase saved nonlinear-scoring work.

One-pass optimization, seed effects and rare positives, especially fav/buy or empty-history slices, can explain small differences. Nonzero OOV collisions and inherited official_offline feedback maturity limit interpretation.
The 32-dimensional shared slot projection may itself discard information; failure of one mean/projection implementation does not rule out learned or task-conditioned compression.

variants.name: target_early
variants.note: Main hypothesis: disjoint category/brand-match slots crossed with older/recent ordinal bands; mean before local activation. Eight slot projections and counts enter each joint context/target/task readout.

variants.name: position_early
variants.note: Replace target-field routing with four position bins in each of the same two recency bands. Same eight slots, parameters, count channels, pointwise local MLP, projections and towers. Simple target-blind compression control.

variants.name: target_late
variants.note: Same target-field slots, but apply local activation to all 100 masked events before slot-wise mean pooling. Full-resolution nonlinear scoring control; no pre-score compression.

variants.name: position_late
variants.note: Target-blind position slots with full-resolution event scoring. Completes the routing x compression-timing factorial; same learnable parameters as every other variant.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Used the prior idea of keeping recent and earlier representations distinct, with explicit comparison against target-blind grouping. Primary v3 and pinned benchmark paths inspected; no local effectiveness is imported.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: Use a shared fixed last16 ordinal split and deterministic category/brand-match groups, rather than mixed learned queries or HeteroMixer. Test moving local nonlinear scoring across group means.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: No fixed/dynamic query attention, real-time day boundary or heterogeneous low-rank token mixer. Exact fixed100 visibility and four task readouts remain shared. This is a prospective adaptation, not novelty or a HeMix reproduction.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: No positive factorial interaction or no measured quality-cost benefit; gains from counts alone would not establish the proposed retention explanation.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Flattened-history tokenization is an alternative to early compression, but no local evidence justifies its large projection and paired-stream complexity for this first compression study. Card and primary benchmark description inspected; original UniMixer paper not audited.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: None; no UniMixer flattening or paired-stream mixing is implemented.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Retain disjoint masked summaries with a small shared projection; no claim of superiority to unrun UniMixer.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: If early summaries lose quality while full-resolution scoring retains it, reconsider a full-information tokenizer under a later parameter/cost-matched proposal.
